page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-96 is a high-memory cloud server built on 64-bit x86 architecture. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 756 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. This near 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio is structured to accommodate workloads that require significant memory capacities per processing thread.

Hardware accelerators are not bundled with this configuration, as the GPU count is zero. Furthermore, local storage is not attached, meaning all disk persistence and I/O operations rely on external network-attached block storage. The instance also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network routing via private subnets or separate address provisioning.

By delivering a high volume of RAM relative to dedicated execution cores, the c4d-highmem-96 avoids the inefficiency of provisioning unnecessary compute capacity simply to acquire sufficient memory. It is suited for in-memory caching solutions, enterprise relational database management systems, large scale data transformation pipelines, and memory-constrained batch analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-96 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 756 GB of system memory. Providing 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, this configuration delivers a near 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no integrated GPU hardware and provides no bundled local disk storage, necessitating remote persistent disks for persistent storage needs. Network configurations also omit complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The substantial memory footprint combined with 96 dedicated processing threads offers operational efficiency for memory-bound systems by avoiding the overhead of deploying excess compute just to satisfy memory requirements. Consequently, c4d-highmem-96 is tailored for large in-memory databases, enterprise in-memory caches, large-scale data analytics, ETL transformations, and memory-heavy enterprise backend workloads.
